bex CLI v0.3.2

Interact with resources on Bex

USAGE
  bex <subcommand> [flags]

SUBCOMMANDS
Core
  deploys              List, create, and cancel deploys
  jobs                 Create and manage one-off jobs
  keyvalues            Manage Bex Key Value instances (alias: kv)
  logs                 View logs for services and datastores
  postgres             Manage Bex Postgres databases (alias: pg)
  restart              Restart a service by resource ID
  services             List services and datastores for the active workspace
  workflows            Manage Bex Workflows in your workspace
  workspaces           List workspaces available to your account

Auth
  login                Log in to Bex using the Bex dashboard
  logout               Log out of Bex
  whoami               Display information about the current user
  workspace            Manage the CLI's active workspace

Session
  kv-cli               Open a session for a Bex Key Value instance
  pgcli                Open a pgcli session to a Bex Postgres database instance
  psql                 Open a psql session to a Bex Postgres database
  ssh                  SSH into a service instance

Management
  blueprints           Manage Blueprints, which define your infrastructure as code
  environments         List project environments by project ID
  projects             List projects in the active workspace

Additional Commands:
  code                 Manage the Bex coding-agent launchers (glm, muse, kimi, deepseek)
  completion           Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  deepseek             Launch Claude Code backed by DeepSeek
  docs                 Open the Bex docs in your browser
  ea                   Use early access commands
  glm                  Launch Claude Code backed by GLM (Z.ai coding plan)
  help                 Help about any command
  kimi                 Launch Claude Code backed by Kimi (Moonshot platform)
  muse                 Launch Claude Code backed by Muse Spark (Meta Model API)
  skills               Manage Bex agent skills for AI coding tools
  upgrade              Update bex to the latest release

FLAGS
      --confirm           Skip all confirmation prompts
  -h, --help              Show help for this command
  -o, --output <FORMAT>   Set output format to interactive, json, yaml, or text. Auto-switches to text on non-TTY (default: "interactive")
  -v, --version           version for bex

EXAMPLES
  # List services in the active workspace
  bex services

  # Output services as JSON
  bex services --output json

DETAILS
Welcome! Use the bex CLI to manage your services, datastores, and environments
directly from the command line. Trigger deploys, view logs, start psql/SSH
sessions, and more.

The CLI's default interactive mode provides intuitive, menu-based navigation.

To use in non-interactive mode (such as in a script), set each command's
--output option to either json or yaml for structured responses. The CLI also
detects non-TTY stdout and automatically switches to text output.


Use "bex <subcommand> --help" for more information about a command.

bex CLI v0.3.2

Create a new Bex Key Value instance

USAGE
  bex keyvalues create [flags]

FLAGS
      --environment <ENVIRONMENT>             Set the environment to create the Key Value in (ID or name, optional). Example: Production or evm-abc123def456
  -h, --help                                  Show help for this command
      --ip-allow-list <CIDR_DESCRIPTION>      Restrict inbound traffic to specific IP ranges (format: cidr=<range>,description=<label>). Repeat the flag for multiple entries
      --memory-policy <MAXMEMORY_POLICY>      Set the eviction policy used when the instance runs out of memory.
Accepts a friendly alias — cache (= allkeys_lru, for caching) or queue (= noeviction, for job queues) —
or any raw policy: noeviction | allkeys_lru | allkeys_lfu | allkeys_random | volatile_lru | volatile_lfu | volatile_random | volatile_ttl
      --name <NAME>                           Set the Key Value instance name (generated if not provided)
      --persistence-mode <PERSISTENCE_MODE>   Set the on-disk persistence mode: journal_snapshot | snapshot | off (off loses data on restart; omit to use the plan default)
      --plan <PLAN>                           Set the plan to one of: free | 256mb | 1g | 5g | 10g | 20g | 40g. Custom enterprise plan names are also accepted
      --project <PROJECT>                     Scope environment lookup to a project (ID or name, optional); if the project has exactly one environment it is used automatically
      --region <REGION>                       Set the region: frankfurt | ohio | oregon | singapore | virginia
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>                 Set the workspace to create the Key Value in (ID or name). Defaults to the active workspace (set via 'bex workspace set')
      --confirm                               Skip all confirmation prompts
  -o, --output <FORMAT>                       Set output format to interactive, json, yaml, or text. Auto-switches to text on non-TTY (default: "interactive")

EXAMPLES
  # Interactive wizard (guided prompts for each option)
  bex kv create

  # Specify all options; wizard still asks for confirmation before creating
  bex kv create --name my-cache --plan 256mb --region oregon

  # Skip all prompts and create immediately (no confirmation)
  bex kv create --name my-cache --plan free --confirm

  # Machine-readable output (non-interactive, no prompts)
  bex kv create --name my-cache --plan 256mb --output json

  # Use as a cache with no on-disk persistence
  bex kv create --name my-cache --plan 256mb --persistence-mode off

  # With IP allow-listing (repeat the flag for multiple entries)
  bex kv create --name my-cache \
    --ip-allow-list "cidr=203.0.113.5/32,description=office" \
    --ip-allow-list "cidr=10.0.0.0/8,description=internal"

DETAILS
Create a new Bex Key Value instance.

In interactive mode, a prompt guides you through each option one at a time.
In non-interactive mode (--output text/json/yaml), flags use defaults if not
supplied.
Use --confirm to skip all prompts (including final confirmation) and create
immediately.
Output will be human-readable; use --output json/yaml/text for machine-readable
output.

bex CLI v0.3.2

Open a session for a Bex Key Value instance

USAGE
  bex kv-cli [keyValueID|keyValueName] [flags]

FLAGS
  -h, --help              Show help for this command
      --confirm           Skip all confirmation prompts
  -o, --output <FORMAT>   Set output format to interactive, json, yaml, or text. Auto-switches to text on non-TTY (default: "interactive")

EXAMPLES
  # Open an interactive kv-cli session
  bex kv-cli kv-abc123

  # Pass through redis-cli arguments
  bex kv-cli kv-abc123 -- --scan

DETAILS
Open a redis-cli or valkey-cli session for a Bex Key Value instance. This
command only supports interactive mode.

You can optionally pass the key value ID or name as an argument. To pass
arguments to redis-cli or valkey-cli, use:
  bex kv-cli [keyValueID|keyValueName] -- [redis-cli args]

bex CLI v0.3.2

Delete a Bex Key Value instance

USAGE
  bex keyvalues delete <keyValueID|keyValueName> [flags]

FLAGS
      --environment <ENVIRONMENT>   Narrow lookup to an environment (ID or name, optional) when the same Key Value name exists in multiple environments
  -h, --help                        Show help for this command
      --confirm                     Skip all confirmation prompts
  -o, --output <FORMAT>             Set output format to interactive, json, yaml, or text. Auto-switches to text on non-TTY (default: "interactive")

EXAMPLES
  # Preview deletion (no changes made)
  bex kv delete red-abc123def456ghi789jkl0

  # Delete by ID
  bex kv delete red-abc123def456ghi789jkl0 --confirm

  # Delete by name
  bex kv delete my-cache --confirm

  # Disambiguate a name that exists in multiple environments
  bex kv delete my-cache --environment production --confirm

  # JSON output
  bex kv delete red-abc123def456ghi789jkl0 --confirm --output json

DETAILS
Delete a Bex Key Value instance.

Without --confirm, this command previews what would be deleted and makes no
changes. Pass --confirm to actually delete the instance.

The positional argument accepts either a Key Value ID (red-...) or a name.
If the name matches more than one instance, narrow the search with
--environment <id|name>, or pass the Key Value ID directly.

Name lookup is scoped to your active workspace. If a name isn't found, switch
workspaces with 'bex workspace set <name|ID>' and try again, or pass the
Key Value ID instead (which works across workspaces).
